ety.text: From Middle English request, from Old French requeste (French requête), from Vulgar Latin *requaesita, from Latin requīsīta, feminine of requīsītus (“requested, demanded”), past participle of requīrō (“require, ask”), composed of re- + quaerō (“to seek, look for”), of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *kʷaizeō, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeh₂- (“to acquire”). Compare to French requérir.

ex: I have requested that the furniture be moved back to its original position.
She called me into her office and requested me to sit down.

senses.d: Act of requesting (with the adposition at in the presence of possessives, and on in their absence).
ex: I will marry her, sir, at your request.
The promise that arises upon an account stated, is to pay on request.

senses.d: A message sent over a network to a server.
ex: The server returned a 404 error to the HTTP request.

senses.d: That which is asked for or requested.

senses.d: To demand, to insist upon (having); to call for authoritatively.
ex: "I am Miss Newbury," I announced, "and I require to be shown to my room immediately, if you please."

senses.d: Naturally to demand (something) as indispensable; to need, to call for as necessary.
ex: Chronic pain is occasionally a sign of a very serious problem, like brain tumors, and can require surgery.
A weapon small enough to put on a missile would require uranium enriched to more than 90% U-235.

senses.d: To demand (of someone) to do something.
ex: It is required (of me) that I give evidence in court.
After Aug 3 all salesgirls will be required to wear only one style of skirt while on duty: the midi.

senses.d: To ask (someone) for something; to request; to beseech.
ex: I requyre the in the name of god, that thou torment me nott.

senses.d: A necessity or prerequisite; something required or obligatory. Its adpositions are generally of in relation to who or what has given it, on in relation to whom or what it is given to, and for in relation to what is required.
ex: Near-synonyms: necessity, prerequisite, requisite, condition, rule
The requirements of life as we know it include carbon, oxygen, hydrogen, water, and energy.

senses.d: A statement (in domain specific terms) which specifies a verifiable constraint on an implementation that it shall undeniably meet or (a) be deemed unacceptable, or (b) result in implementation failure, or (c) result in system failure.
ex: System requirements not met. Go to Settings to learn more.
